question.text: How many seats will PP and Vox collectively receive in the 2026 Spanish general election?
question.resolution_criteria: This question will resolve as the total number of seats in the Congress of Deputies won by either the People's Party or Vox in the [2026 Spanish general election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Spanish_general_election), scheduled to be held on November 29, 2026. The question resolves according to official results or [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions).
question.fine_print:
If election results are not available before January 1, 2027, this question will be **annulled**.

***
This question's information (resolution criteria, fine print, background info, etc) is synced with an [original identical question](https://www.metaculus.com/questions/46036) which opened on 2026-10-18 17:00:00. However, if this question would resolve differently than the original question, then this question will be annulled. Additionally, if the original question's resolution could have been known before this question opened, then this question will be annulled.

research:
## 1. Resolution source
- The question resolves on official Congress results for the 29 November 2026 election, using the Wikipedia page as the reference. Majority is 176 of 350 seats.
- 2026-10-25: The Wikipedia page confirms the date, and that the Cortes were dissolved on 6 Oct. PP runs with UPN and Foro Asturias; Vox runs alone. No results exist yet. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Spanish_general_election)
- Seat counts at dissolution: PP 138 (137 won in 2023), Vox 33. The 2023 PP+Vox total was 170.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question. The vote is in 5 weeks. Every private poll puts PP+Vox at about 195 to 212 seats, comfortably over 176. The government-run CIS pollster is the exception.
- One collected news item describes a "July 2026 election" with PP+Vox at 170. This is a mislabel of the 23 July 2023 election. [Periodista Digital](https://www.periodistadigital.com/politica/partidos-politicos/20261024/9-provincias-le-escapo-pelo-victoria-centroderecha-2023-10-quese-juega-29-n-noticia-689405259895/)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-10-25: El Debate's compilation of 12 pollsters (fieldwork 6 Sep to 9 Oct) gives PP+Vox 198 to 212, median 203. Ranges: PP 129 to 147, Vox 62 to 70, PSOE 100 to 112. The CIS's only seat estimate (March 2026) gave PP+Vox 162. [El Debate](https://www.eldebate.com/espana/20261025/dicen-ultimas-encuestas-sobre-elecciones-generales-29-noviembre-cns_472138.html)
- 2026-10-25: Periodista Digital reports the DatosRTVE average at PP 135, about 20 seats over a majority for PP+Vox (roughly 196). [Periodista Digital](https://www.periodistadigital.com/politica/parlamento/20261025/barometro-29-n-pronostican-encuestas-cinco-semanas-elecciones-generales-noticia-689405260131/)
- 2026-10-25: El Confidencial/CIDOB discuss a scenario of PP about 125 and Vox about 70. [El Confidencial](https://www.elconfidencial.com/espana/mientras-tanto/2026-10-25/peor-escenario-posibles-estabilidad-politica_4452355/)
- 2026-10-25: PP and Vox are negotiating Senate-only cooperation (deadline 26 Oct for lists). It does not affect Congress lists. [20minutos](https://www.20minutos.es/nacional/pp-vox-apuran-los-plazos-para-lograr-un-acuerdo-senado-que-les-permita-atar-una-mayoria-suficiente-contra-izquierda_7052499_0.html)
- 2026-10-24: The Objective/Redlines "Votómetro" has PP 139 (32.2%), Vox 68 (18.4%), PSOE 105, FA 10. Combined: 207. Headline: "PSOE and Vox grow at PP's expense". [The Objective](https://theobjective.com/espana/politica/2026-10-24/psoe-vox-crece-pp-pierde-votometro/)
- 2026-10-23: IMOP/El Confidencial has PP 123 (28.5%), Vox 72, PSOE 113 (27.1%), FA 14. Combined: 195, down 6 from two weeks earlier. It is the lowest PP figure among private polls. [Electomanía](https://electomania.es/encuesta-imop-23-oct-psoe-y-fa-recortan-12-escanos-a-pp-y-vox/), [Demócrata](https://www.democrata.es/encuestas/elecciones-generales/encuesta-elecciones-generales-imop-psoe-frente-amplio-vox-pp-octubre-2026/)
- 2026-10-22: The poll average (elDiario.es, 10,000 simulations) gives PP 133, Vox 65, PSOE 105, for 198 combined. A CIS-based calculation gives PP 119 and PSOE 116. [Moncloa.com](https://www.moncloa.com/2026/10/22/encuestas-pp-vox-198-escanos-29n-3453350/)
- 2026-10-14: The CIS barometer puts PSOE at 34.0% and PP at 22.2%. It is a strong outlier. [El Debate](https://www.eldebate.com/espana/20261025/dicen-ultimas-encuestas-sobre-elecciones-generales-29-noviembre-cns_472138.html)
- 2026-10-11/12: SocioMétrica/El Español has PP 32.6%, Vox 18.8%, PSOE 26.2%, about 141+64=205 seats. Write-ups disagree: PolitPro lists PP 137 and Vox 79. An earlier SocioMétrica gave 207. [Electográfica](https://www.electografica.com/2026/10/encuesta-sociometrica-261012.html), [PolitPro](https://politpro.eu/es/espana/intencion-de-voto/sociometrica-2026-10-11/elecciones-parlamentarias), [Demócrata](https://www.democrata.es/encuestas/elecciones-generales/encuesta-elecciones-generales-vox-gana-5-escanos-psoe-recupera-4-pp-vox-alcanzan-207-segun-sociometrica/)
- Trend: the most recent polls (IMOP, Votómetro) suggest PSOE and Vox are gaining slightly and PP is slipping. The combined bloc is easing from about 201 to 207 toward about 195 to 207.

## 4. Base rates
- PP+Vox seats in past elections: April 2019 about 90 (66+24); November 2019 141 (89+52); 2023 170 (137+33).
- 2023 polling error: from memory, final polls averaged roughly 175 to 183 for PP+Vox, against an actual 170. That is an overestimate of about 5 to 13 seats, and the PSOE outperformed. I did not re-verify this in this session.
- Spread across current pollsters is about 195 to 212, roughly ±8 around the median of 198 to 203. The CIS-implied scenario is far lower, around 160s or below.
- D'Hondt with small provinces magnifies seat swings. El Debate noted nine provinces where the 2023 right-bloc seat outcome was decided by narrow margins.

## 5. Other forecasts
- Kalshi, PP+Vox at least 50% of the vote: 41% Yes. Vox vote share: at least 18% at 56%, at least 19% at 44%, at least 20% at 28%. The median is roughly 18.5%, consistent with polls.
- Polymarket winner (most seats): PP 77.5%, PSOE 21%. 3rd place: Vox 91.5%.
- Kalshi "winner (in 2027)": PP 41%, PSOE 24%. This is likely a different contract definition, so check it before relying on it.
- I found no market on combined PP+Vox seats, and no Metaculus community figure.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- 2026-10-26: Deadline for candidate lists. Vox presents its head candidates in Talavera. The PP-Vox Senate pact decision is due.
- November: Official campaign (typically starting about 15 days before the vote, around 13 Nov), TV debates (dates not found), and further polls including a CIS pre-election macro-survey. Spanish law bans publishing polls in the final 5 days (from about 24 Nov).
- Ongoing issues: the housing protests, migration after the Ceuta crisis, the corruption probes (Koldo and Zapatero), and the Iran war base controversy.
- 2026-11-29: Election. The provisional count is normally available that night.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) About 5 weeks remain. The election is on 29 November 2026, and the provisional count should be known that night.

(b) There are no results yet. The latest reference value is the 2023 result, PP 137 plus Vox 33, which totals 170 seats (PP held 138 at dissolution). Current private polls, as of 22 to 25 October 2026, put PP+Vox at about 195 to 212 seats, with a median of about 198 to 203.

(c) If the polls held exactly as they are, PP+Vox would get roughly 198 to 203 seats.

(d) The latest polls, IMOP at 195 and the Votómetro at 207, show PSOE and Vox gaining slightly and PP slipping. If that drift continues, the combined bloc ends up around 192 to 198.

(e) In Spain, the final weeks of a campaign can move bloc totals by 10 seats or more. In 2023 the polls overestimated PP+Vox by roughly 5 to 13 seats, and PSOE outperformed. D'Hondt seat allocation in small provinces exaggerates these swings. The spread across current pollsters is about ±8 seats.

(f) Markets:
- Kalshi gives PP+Vox only a 41% chance of reaching 50% of the vote, which suggests a combined vote just under 50%.
- Kalshi's implied median Vox share is about 18.5%.
- Polymarket gives PP a 77.5% chance of winning the most seats.
- The poll aggregates are 196 (DatosRTVE) and 198 (elDiario.es).
- The CIS is an outlier, pointing to the 160s.

Taken together, the market prices are consistent with a median of about 195 to 198 seats.

(g) Scenarios:
- **Low:** A late PSOE surge on housing, a repeat of the 2023 mobilisation against Vox, and errors in the same direction as 2023 push the bloc down to about 175 to 180.
- **High:** PSOE collapses after the corruption probes (Koldo, Zapatero) and immigration dominates the campaign. Then PP+Vox reach about 50 to 52% of the vote and 210 or more seats.

(d) If the current trend continued, the bloc would keep easing (IMOP 195, PSOE recovering, PP slipping, Vox stable). That points to roughly 190 to 196 by election day.

(f) Experts and markets:

- High: the Ceuta and corruption stories dominate the campaign, Vox reaches 20% or more, and PP holds 140. The bloc reaches 215 or more.
